answer: Inter-arrival jitter gating. Each identity must submit its first N actions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a shared reference kernel of plausible human timing; gaps outside tolerance are rejected at ingest. The trellis of accepted timestamps per identity is committed, so parallel identities cannot share one schedule without collision. Each extra identity therefore costs a dedicated operator sleeping through realistic delays, multiplying attacker wall-clock time and labor linearly. A fable of effortless scale fails.
